sections.h2: Three ways to sell a Bryan house
sections.html:
A Bryan seller can use an agent, go solo, or take cash. Let the house's condition and the time you have drive the decision. An agent listing means cleanup, open houses and a closing that depends on the buyer's lender. Cash skips all of that, in exchange for a price that discounts repairs and risk.

Selling without an agent means you set the price, field the calls and work the contract through a title company yourself. That saves a commission, but it only works for someone at ease screening buyers and reading a contract line by line.

Before choosing, compare two figures on paper: your probable net from a listing after costs and waiting, and the cash offer with a fixed closing date.

The city has more than 93,000 people and shares Brazos County with College Station and Texas A&M. Long-time families, university staff, students and renters all shape who shows up to buy or lease a house here.

Rail service came in 1867 and Bryan incorporated November 29, 1871. The oldest houses stand near historic downtown, and an inspector will go straight to the wiring, plumbing and foundation. Electric service comes from the city's own Bryan Texas Utilities, so call the utility office about final readings and transferring service on closing day.

Brazos Central Appraisal District values each parcel, then each taxing unit serving it sets a rate. Use the calendar below to see who owes what at closing.

Yearly sequence for Brazos County property tax
WindowWhat happens
January 1Parcel is assessed as of this date
April through MayAppraisal notices go out in several mailings from April 15 to June 1
May 15 or 30 days after noticeLast day to protest the value
July through SeptemberCity, county, school and special districts set their rates
October and NovemberBills come from the assessor-collector

You can reach the district at 4051 Pendleton Dr. in Bryan or 979-774-4100. A year's tax is secured on January 1. Whatever remains unpaid after January 31 is delinquent. If you close in fall or winter, that year's bill is typically still open, and the settlement statement must say who pays it. Rates shift annually, so ask the Brazos County tax office for each unit's current figure.

If you live in the house, the residence homestead exemption takes $140,000 off the value used for school taxes. Older and disabled owners receive more school relief and a tax ceiling. Ask Brazos CAD whether a service-connected disability earns a veteran a separate exemption.

  • Send exemption applications to the district by email. Staff answer phones on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Zoom details for appraisal review board hearings are posted on the district's tax process page.

A value dispute goes to the appraisal review board, which has an email address of its own. Certain properties, undivided-interest ownership among them, can't use the online appeals portal. If yours is one, phone the district well ahead of the deadline.

sections.h2: Selling a house that was a short-term rental
sections.html:
Rent a Bryan home, apartment or garage unit for 30 days or less and it counts as a short-term rental. Hotel occupancy tax of 7 percent applies to the gross rent, including cleaning and pet charges.

  • Returns are filed through the GovOS portal, due monthly by the 20th of the next month.
  • Owners who owe under $500 a month or $1,500 a quarter can file quarterly.
  • A quarter with no bookings still needs a zero return.
  • To close an account, email the GovOS support address with the closure date and reason.

File your last returns before handing over the keys, so no tax balance follows you. The city's fiscal services office answers questions at 979-209-5080. Tell any buyer whether guests are already booked for future dates.

sections.h2: Inherited, behind on payments or rented?
sections.html:
Each of these has its own timeline.

After an owner's death, expect the title insurer to want a court order or a sworn affidavit first. The state law library outlines three routes, and each takes different paperwork.

Behind on the loan? The servicer's default letter gives you 20 days to catch up. After that a notice of sale must be posted 21 or more days before the courthouse auction. Selling first can protect your equity.

If a tenant lives there, the first step is a written notice to vacate, usually three days, and a court filing comes next. An as-is buyer takes over wherever the case stands.

Old tax doesn't disappear when you sell. It clings to the land, so it has to be paid from your proceeds or the buyer inherits it. Phone the Brazos County tax office for the exact payoff before you weigh offers, and mentally subtract it from every number you hear. Delinquent balances keep growing after January 31, so ask early.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Brazos County
sections.html:
Recording is done by the Brazos County clerk, so that is where the deed for a Bryan lot is filed. Before it records a conveyance, the clerk needs either a notary's acknowledgment or two witnesses.

The Texas courts' 2023 clerk manual sets one fee for the first page, a smaller one per added page, and several extras. The clerk can give you the current total. Your title company usually does the recording and sends you the copy.

sections.h2: What to line up before a cash closing
sections.html:
Pull together your latest tax bill, the mortgage payoff, any lease, and rental tax filings if guests stayed. Heirs bring probate or affidavit paperwork, and an heir who isn't on the deed must also show the appraisal district an ownership interest before claiming an exemption. With these papers in hand, a buyer can name a price and a closing date quickly. If students or other renters live in the house under a lease, a buyer will ask for that lease first, along with its end date.

Once an offer is signed, the title company looks for liens and open taxes, while you settle the closing date and request final meter readings from the utility office. At closing, tax proration and any loan payoff come out of your proceeds, a notary witnesses the deed signature, and the clerk files it. Keep the settlement statement with your tax records and cancel your own insurance afterward.

faqs.q: How fast can a Bryan house sale close?
faqs.a: A cash sale with clean title can be done in a few weeks, because no lender has to sign off. Listing takes longer because the buyer's loan and appraisal set the clock. Either path slows down for an unprobated estate or an open lien.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a Bryan house sells?
faqs.a: Buyer and seller normally share the sale year's tax, as shown on the settlement statement. Any earlier unpaid year gets paid at closing, since that lien stays on the land. Call the Brazos County tax office for your balance.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bryan house that is listed on Airbnb?
faqs.a: Yes. File your hotel occupancy tax returns first, because the city requires monthly or quarterly reports on short-term rent. Tell buyers if future dates are already booked.

faqs.q: Do I need to probate before selling an inherited house in Bryan?
faqs.a: Usually, unless another recorded route shows who has authority. Choices include a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or an administration.

faqs.q: What can I do if a Bryan foreclosure sale is scheduled?
faqs.a: Move before the first Tuesday sale. You can reinstate within 20 days of the default notice, sell the house, or talk to the servicer about alternatives. After an auction, leftover equity goes to junior lienholders before it reaches you.
